cards.text: Job, the man from the land of Uz (Job 1:1), has just finished speaking. Now Bildad the Shuhite, one of his friends (Job 2:11), replies. He opens BIG: dominion and awe belong to God, and He establishes harmony in the heights of heaven.

cards.question: Bildad asks how many troops God has, and then he asks a question about God's light. What is Bildad's point about God's light?
Then Bildad turns from God to people. What does Bildad ask about people?

answers.text: Whether anyone can be right before God
Whether anyone can hide from God
Whether anyone can see God's face

cards.text: Then Bildad points to the night sky: if even the moon does not shine and the stars are not pure in His sight... Friend, I scrape one smudge off a cookie and call it perfect, and Bildad says the STARS don't pass inspection.

cards.question: True or false: Bildad says that compared to the moon and the stars, man looks more pure in God's sight.

cards.text: Bildad says how much less man, who is 'but a maggot,' and the son of man, who is 'but a worm!' Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and on my worst day back there I'd have taken 'worm' as a PROMOTION.
And just like that, Bildad is done. Then Job answers.

cards.question: Speaking to the one he's answering, Job says that person has saved the arm that is feeble and helped the ___.

cards.text: Then Job says, 'How you have counseled the unwise and provided fully sound insight!' I bet that's the same voice you use when your GPS says 'recalculating' for the fifth time: 'WOW. SO helpful.'

cards.question: Job asks the one who just spoke, 'To whom have you uttered these words? And whose spirit spoke through you?' What is Job questioning?

answers.text: When those words were first written
How long those words will go on

cards.text: Now Job talks about God's power, and he starts at the very bottom: the dead tremble, those beneath the waters and those who dwell in them.

cards.question: Job talks about Sheol, the place of the dead, and Abaddon, a place of destruction, and how they stand before God. What does he say about Sheol?

answers.text: It is too deep for Him

cards.text: Then Job looks up: God stretches out the north over empty space. Friend, I can't stretch out one sheet of cookie dough without it tearing in the middle.

cards.question: Job says God hangs the earth upon ___.

cards.text: The whole EARTH, hanging on nothing at all. Then Job points up at the clouds, where God wraps up the waters.

cards.question: True or false: Job says the clouds God wraps the waters in burst under their own weight.

cards.text: Job brings up the moon too, like Bildad did. God covers the face of the full moon, spreading His cloud over it.

cards.question: Job says God has inscribed a horizon on the face of the waters. Where does Job say that line sits?
Job opened his tour of God's power by saying the dead tremble. Now he gets to the foundations of heaven. True or false: Job says the foundations of heaven quake at God's rebuke.

cards.text: The foundations of heaven QUAKE, astounded at His rebuke, and I jump when my oven timer beeps. Then Job says God stirred the sea by His power, and by His understanding He shattered Rahab (not the Rahab of Jericho in Joshua 2:1).

cards.question: Job adds that by His breath the skies were cleared, and His hand pierced the fleeing serpent. What do all the things Job lists here have in common?
After everything Job just listed about God's power, how much does Job say all of it shows of God's ways?

cards.text: Then Job says, '…how faint is the whisper we hear of Him! Who then can understand the thunder of His power?'
All of THAT was just the whisper, friend. And trust me, this story isn't over.
